page: Google Cloud Platform c4d-highmem-32 is a memory-optimized server instance featuring 32 vCPUs and 252 GB of RAM. Powered by an AMD EPYC 9B45 processor with an x86_64 architecture, the instance provides 16 dedicated physical cores with 2 threads per core. The CPU is equipped with 48 KB L1d cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache. It supports advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 (AVX512F, AVX512_VNNI, AVX512_BF16) and cryptographic acceleration via AES and SHA_NI. This instance does not include local storage or GPUs, and provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data shows top-tier performance (top 10%) in single-core CPU execution, single-threaded gzip compression, and single-threaded bzip3 decompression. Geekbench testing places both single-core and multi-core scores in the top 10%, alongside image and text processing workloads. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, software compilation with Clang, ray tracing, and PassMark CPU metrics fall into the strong category (top 25%). However, multi-core stress-ng performance, database operations, and Redis SET operations are average, indicating a potential bottleneck in highly parallelized, memory-bound transactional workloads.

With approximately 7.88 GB of RAM per vCPU, the c4d-highmem-32 offers a high memory-to-core ratio suitable for memory-intensive applications without the overhead of a GPU. The qualitative cost efficiency is driven by its dedicated AMD EPYC cores and high memory density, making it a viable option for memory-bound tasks that do not require local NVMe storage. Appropriate workloads include software compilation, text and image processing, static web serving, and small-scale LLM inference, where its top-tier single-core performance and strong memory score can be fully utilized.
